mechanism_narrative: The sharp rise in PARKS mobility alongside lower WORKPLACES and only mildly lower TRANSIT signals a shift toward discretionary out-of-home activity that spills into shopping trips. That mix should raise RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as leisure outings convert into retail visits.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed its prior 4-week mean over the next 28 days even while PARKS stays above the snapshot average and WORKPLACES remains below it.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM rises above 15 points, households are already making more errand trips and nearby retail visits follow with a short lag. This implies a one-week to two-week increase in RETAIL_REC after the threshold is crossed.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within 7 to 14 days after GROCERY_PHARM exceeds 15 points, or falls instead.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM indicates a broader recreation-and-errands rebound that is stronger than either series alone. If both remain elevated, RETAIL_REC should increase over the next two weeks through bundled outing behavior.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 14 days despite both PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM staying above their recent means.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT continues to sit more than 15 points below baseline, access friction suppresses spontaneous shopping trips and RETAIL_REC stays depressed. This mechanism should hold for a four-week horizon unless transit recovery occurs.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days while TRANSIT stays below -15 points for most of the period.

mechanism_narrative: A further rise in RESIDENTIAL mobility above 4 points signals stronger stay-at-home substitution, which should divert time away from retail and recreation. The effect should appear within two weeks and lower RETAIL_REC relative to the recent baseline.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within 14 days after RESIDENTIAL rises above 4 points.

mechanism_narrative: An acceleration in WORKPLACES combined with flat or falling RESIDENTIAL mobility marks a return to away-from-home routines that feeds discretionary shopping over the following month. The retail effect should be positive only when commuting intensity and home-stay intensity move in opposite directions.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its prior 4-week mean over the next 28 days even as WORKPLACES rises and RESIDENTIAL falls or stays flat.

mechanism_narrative: A surge in PARKS mobility above 40 points reflects a short-run leisure spike that diverts trips toward outdoor activities instead of shops. In this regime the effect should be a one-week dip in RETAIL_REC, not a delayed increase.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises within 7 days after PARKS exceeds 40 points.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT improves while WORKPLACES remains below baseline, access to commercial areas recovers before office demand does, producing a delayed retail upswing. The mechanism should lift RETAIL_REC over four weeks only in this partial-reopening pattern.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by at least 3 points while WORKPLACES stays below 0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next 28 days when TRANSIT rises and WORKPLACES remains below baseline.
